question: In Newlands’ octaves, which of the following pairs of elements were placed in the same column along with H, F, Cl and Br?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Co and Ni**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Newlands placed cobalt and nickel in the same slot and positioned them in the same column with fluorine, chlorine and bromine that possess different properties compared to these two elements (Cobalt and Nickel).
 
• This is one of the demerits of Newland's law of octaves.
 
• In Newlands' Octaves, elements were arranged in such a way that similar elements were placed in the same column (group), based on increasing atomic masses. Newlands observed that every eighth element had similar chemical properties, resembling the pattern of musical octaves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• C and K (Carbon and Potassium)
 
 
• Carbon (C) and Potassium (K) do not share similar chemical properties, and they were not placed in the same column in Newlands’ octaves.
 
• Carbon is a non-metal, and potassium is an alkali metal, so this pair does not fit.
 
 
 
• Cr and Zr (Chromium and Zirconium)
 
 
• Chromium (Cr) and Zirconium (Zr) are transition metals but are not placed in the same column in Newlands’ octaves.
 
• Chromium and Zirconium have distinct properties, and Newlands didn’t group them together.
 
 
 
• P and S (Phosphorus and Sulfur)
 
 
• Phosphorus (P) and Sulfur (S) are non-metals and share similar chemical properties as they belong to the same group in the modern periodic table (Group 16).
 
• However, in Newlands' arrangement, they were not placed in the same column as H, F, Cl, and Br because of the nature of Newlands' grouping based on atomic mass and chemical behavior, which doesn’t perfectly align with the modern periodic table.
